title: A 4X Mobile Game Made with AI
author: FewEntertainment9716
selftext:
​

Good morning everyone!

I know I'm probably going to get some criticism for this, but I'm currently developing—or at least trying to develop—a 4X mobile game using AI.

Of course, I would have preferred to have real human artists working on the project, but unfortunately I simply don't have the budget for that, apart from what I'm already paying for my AI subscription.

I'm a huge fan of this genre, and that's exactly why I decided to take on this challenge.

I've been working on the game for four months now, so even though AI makes certain things much easier, it's definitely not as simple as some people might think. I'm still quite far from having a finished product, and I estimate it will take another four months or so.

I know it might sound like all you have to do is tell the AI what to do and it does everything for you. And to some extent, that's true.

However, when you're working on a project of this scale, things get much more complicated. For example, handling all the game's calculations in real time on the server side is a massive challenge. Currently, the game is completely server-authoritative, with everything handled server-side, and I've designed it to be as secure as possible against hacking and cheating.

AI also frequently makes mistakes and hallucinates, especially when dealing with complex systems like these. As a result, I've had to rebuild, review, and fix many parts of the game over and over again.

I'm genuinely interested in hearing your opinions.

I already know that some people will probably criticize me for using AI, but personally, I believe we're reaching a point where we need to accept that AI can now help accomplish work that would previously have required entire teams and years of development.

What do you guys think?

comments.author: Accomplished-Cat5451
comments.body: I don't mean to criticize you for using AI it's a great tool in itself but the issue is that the visuals in your game just don't fit together. The UI, that green grass background, the items, and the character designs... it all feels inconsistent and unpolished.

replies.author: FewEntertainment9716
replies.body:
Yeah, I've definitely seen worse. Just look at Evony, for example. It's a mix of generals, dragons, beasts, and all sorts of different things. Even King of Avalon introduced the White Walkers from Game of Thrones, which feel completely out of place, and yet these are among the top games in the genre.

At least my game has a consistent purple and gold color scheme, with a recurring eclipse theme. The sprites are also designed to reflect that theme.

Obviously, I can't achieve the same level of art direction as a professional studio when I'm working alone and relying on AI.

And of course, there's still a lot of work to be done in terms of visual consistency, especially when it comes to the menus and user interface.

But personally, I actually really like the heroes and deities I've created, and I don't think the dragon looks bad either.

I'll always admit that AI-generated art lacks some of the soul and personal touch that a human artist could bring to a project. Unfortunately, that's one of the limitations I have to accept given my circumstances.
